story_description: Enable exporting hook configurations from the visual builder to various target formats, allowing users to share, backup, and deploy hooks across different CLI providers and plugin systems.
task_description: Create HookExportService actor that handles exporting hook configurations to multiple formats including Claude settings.json, Gemini settings.json, plugin hooks.json, and YAML frontmatter for agents/skills.
atom_description: Implement HookExportService actor with ExportFormat enum supporting claudeSettings, geminiSettings, pluginHooks, and frontmatter formats. Provides async export method with pre-export validation via HookValidator, format-specific exporters, and intelligent merging with existing settings files to preserve non-hook configuration.
problem_statement: Users who create hooks in the visual builder need to export them for actual use with CLI tools. Each CLI provider expects hooks in different formats: Claude uses .claude/settings.json with a hooks object, Gemini uses .gemini/settings.json with its own schema, plugins expect hooks.json with wrapper metadata, and agent/skill definitions use YAML frontmatter. Currently there is no unified export mechanism that validates configurations before export, handles format conversion correctly, and safely merges with existing settings files without clobbering non-hook configuration.

assumptions: HookConfiguration type exists with toJSON() method that returns JSON-compatible dictionary
HookValidator type exists with validate(config:) async method returning ValidationResult
ValidationResult has isValid boolean and errors array properties
File paths provided to export are writable by the application
Existing settings files are valid JSON that can be parsed and re-serialized
Users understand the different export formats and their use cases
Pretty-printed JSON is preferred over compact JSON for settings files
YAML frontmatter uses standard --- delimiters and is valid YAML
Gemini CLI uses a hooks schema similar to Claude but may differ in specifics
constraints: Actor isolation required for all file operations to prevent data races
Must not clobber non-hook configuration when merging with existing files
Must validate configuration before any file operations to fail fast
JSON serialization must use sortedKeys for deterministic output and easier diffing
File writes must be atomic to prevent corruption on interruption
Error messages must be specific enough for users to diagnose and fix issues
No third-party dependencies; use Foundation JSONSerialization and FileManager only
Must handle unicode characters correctly in hook prompts and messages
Export to read-only paths must fail with descriptive error, not crash
Minimum macOS 13.0 deployment target for async/await and actor support
functional_requirements: FR1: HookExportService shall be defined as an actor to ensure thread-safe file operations
FR2: ExportFormat enum shall include cases claudeSettings, geminiSettings, pluginHooks, and frontmatter
FR3: export method shall validate configuration using HookValidator before any export operation
FR4: export method shall throw HookExportError.validationFailed(errors) if validation fails
FR5: exportClaudeSettings shall read existing file if present, parse as JSON, update hooks key only, and write back
FR6: exportClaudeSettings shall create new file with hooks key if file does not exist
FR7: exportGeminiSettings shall transform hook configuration to Gemini-compatible schema
FR8: exportPluginHooks shall wrap configuration in plugin metadata including version and author fields
FR9: exportFrontmatter shall generate valid YAML frontmatter block between --- delimiters
FR10: All file writes shall use atomic write option to prevent partial file corruption
FR11: JSON output shall use prettyPrinted and sortedKeys options for readability
FR12: Export shall fail with invalidPath error if path is not writable
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Export operation shall complete within 500ms for typical hook configuration (under 50 hooks)
NFR2: Memory usage during export shall not exceed 10MB including file buffers
NFR3: Actor shall handle concurrent export requests without deadlock or data corruption
NFR4: Error messages shall include file path and specific failure reason
NFR5: Exported JSON shall be valid and parseable by target CLI tools
NFR6: YAML frontmatter output shall be valid YAML parseable by standard YAML parsers
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create new file HookExportService.swift in Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/ directory
Step 2: Define ExportFormat enum with cases claudeSettings, geminiSettings, pluginHooks, frontmatter
Step 3: Define HookExportError enum with cases validationFailed([ValidationError]), fileWriteError(Error), mergeConflict(String), invalidPath(URL)
Step 4: Declare HookExportService as public actor
Step 5: Implement public export(config:format:to:) async throws method as entry point
Step 6: Add validation call at start of export method with early throw on failure
Step 7: Implement switch on format to dispatch to private format-specific methods
Step 8: Implement exportClaudeSettings that reads existing file using Data(contentsOf:)
Step 9: Parse existing data with JSONSerialization.jsonObject to get mutable dictionary
Step 10: Update hooks key with config.toJSON() result, preserving all other keys
Step 11: Serialize updated dictionary with JSONSerialization.data using prettyPrinted and sortedKeys
Step 12: Write output data using write(to:options:.atomic) for safe atomic write
Step 13: Implement exportGeminiSettings with Gemini-specific schema transformation
Step 14: Implement exportPluginHooks that wraps config in plugin metadata dictionary
Step 15: Add plugin metadata fields: version (1.0), author (Blaze), exportedAt (ISO8601 timestamp)
Step 16: Implement exportFrontmatter that converts config to YAML string
Step 17: Format YAML with --- delimiters and proper indentation for frontmatter block
Step 18: Add comprehensive documentation comments for all public types and methods
Step 19: Handle file permission errors with specific HookExportError.invalidPath
Step 20: Add unit tests for each export format and error case

api_contracts: HookExportService.export(config: HookConfiguration, format: ExportFormat, to path: URL) async throws - main export entry point, validates then exports
ExportFormat.claudeSettings - exports to .claude/settings.json format with hooks object
ExportFormat.geminiSettings - exports to .gemini/settings.json format with Gemini schema
ExportFormat.pluginHooks - exports to hooks.json with plugin wrapper metadata
ExportFormat.frontmatter - exports to YAML frontmatter block for agent/skill files
HookExportError.validationFailed - thrown when config fails validation, contains error array
HookExportError.fileWriteError - thrown when file system operation fails, wraps underlying error
HookExportError.mergeConflict - thrown when existing file cannot be safely merged
HookExportError.invalidPath - thrown when path is not writable or invalid

edge_cases: Edge case 1: Existing settings.json is not valid JSON - throw mergeConflict with parse error details
Edge case 2: Existing settings.json has hooks key with incompatible structure - overwrite with warning log
Edge case 3: Export path is a directory instead of file - throw invalidPath with descriptive message
Edge case 4: Export path does not exist but parent directory is writable - create new file successfully
Edge case 5: Export path parent directory does not exist - throw invalidPath suggesting parent creation
Edge case 6: Hook configuration is empty (no hooks) - export successfully with empty hooks array
Edge case 7: Hook prompt contains special JSON characters (quotes, backslashes) - escape correctly in output
Edge case 8: Hook prompt contains unicode emoji or special characters - preserve correctly in UTF-8 output
Edge case 9: File system becomes read-only during write - throw fileWriteError with permission message
Edge case 10: Concurrent exports to same file - actor serializes operations, second waits for first
failure_modes: FM1: Validation failure before export - display specific validation errors, no file operations performed
FM2: File read failure on existing settings - display read error, suggest checking file permissions
FM3: JSON parse failure on existing settings - display parse error with line number if available
FM4: File write failure due to permissions - display permission denied error with path
FM5: File write failure due to disk full - display disk space error with required space estimate
FM6: Atomic write failure (temp file creation) - display temporary file error with temp directory path
FM7: YAML generation failure for frontmatter - display YAML serialization error with offending content
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/HookExportService.swift file. Remove any imports of HookExportService from other files. If export was used to create settings files, those files remain on disk but are standalone and do not affect application state. No database changes to rollback. The export feature is additive and its removal does not break existing functionality.

risks: Risk 1: Merge with existing settings.json may corrupt file if JSON parsing fails midway
Risk 2: Gemini settings schema may differ from documented format, causing invalid exports
Risk 3: YAML frontmatter generation may produce invalid YAML for complex hook configurations
Risk 4: Atomic write may fail silently on certain file systems leaving temp files behind
Risk 5: Unicode handling differences between JSONSerialization and target CLI parsers
mitigations: Mitigation 1: Read and validate existing file completely before any modifications, fail fast on parse error
Mitigation 2: Test Gemini export against actual Gemini CLI, document any schema differences discovered
Mitigation 3: Use simple YAML subset for frontmatter, escape special characters conservatively
Mitigation 4: Clean up temp files in defer block, log warning if cleanup fails
Mitigation 5: Use UTF-8 encoding explicitly throughout, test with emoji and non-ASCII in hook prompts
risk_register.blast_radius: Limited to export functionality. Export failure does not affect existing hook configurations or visual builder. Users can manually create settings files as fallback.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If export proves unreliable, provide a copy-to-clipboard option that shows the JSON/YAML for users to paste manually. No data loss possible as export is write-only operation.
